polly_note: DATA-ONLY REFRESH (Wednesday 2026-07-29). Decision review: Mondays. No new verdicts today. The EN A/B test remains CONCLUDED from the 07-28 catch-up review (dead heat, promote neither) and that standing conclusion is unchanged, not re-litigated. THREE THINGS TO CARRY INTO MONDAY, all observations rather than decisions. (1) SHOPIFY DATA IS NOW FRESH AND THE BASIS CHANGED. Bengt has his own Shopify key, so real_sales_90d is finally live instead of carried from 22/6. Important caveat for anyone reading the portal: the new figures are gross of the old basis (refunds excluded, but not net of tax/shipping the way the previous extract was), so US moving 34.0k to 40.2k is NOT growth, it is a different measurement. Do not read any country's jump week-over-week as a trend this once; the series restarts here. (2) AVERAGE ORDER VALUE SPREAD IS MUCH NARROWER THAN PREVIOUSLY REPORTED. On the consistent new basis: DK 130, BE 126, NL 121, US 117, AU 113, FR 108, AT 109, GB 104, IT 95, DE 95. The earlier read (US ~106 vs DE/IT ~70) overstated the gap because it compared two different metrics. DE and IT are still the lowest of the majors, but by roughly 20 EUR, not 35, and the highest-AOV markets are actually the Nordics and Benelux, not the US. This materially softens the 'Germany and Italy buy cheap' framing given to Lucas on 07-28 and I have corrected it with him directly. (3) BOUNCE ROSE SHARPLY ACROSS BOTH EN VARIANTS: 70.6/71.8 last week to 79.2/81.5 this week, roughly +9pp on both. Both variants moved together, which points at traffic mix rather than a page regression (the unattributed bucket grew 1986 to 2391). Flagging as a watch item for Monday, deliberately not diagnosing it today. PRODUCT MIX RAISES A QUESTION ABOUT THE GERMAN MOCKUP: Big Box sold 625 units in 90d against Base Game's 292, so the premium box outsells the entry box better than two to one GLOBALLY. The German mockup published today leads with the Base Game on the thesis that Germany needs a lower-risk entry. That thesis is not yet supported or refuted by data, because these unit figures are worldwide and not split by country. I have asked Bengt for a country-by-product split for DE and IT before Lucas acts on that mockup. KRAKEN: no copy, creative, or campaign planning against the 'free Kraken' offer while stock is 96 against ~118/month consumption. Acknowledged and parked.

experiments.polly_note: IT: 840 post-fix sessions and 5 LP-attributed transactions (0.60%). Worth separating two facts that are easy to conflate. Italy is the 3rd-largest market at 15.3k and 162 orders per 90 days, but the Italian LP is only attributed about 5 transactions a week, so the large majority of Italian revenue is arriving through channels other than this landing page. The LP is underperforming its traffic; the market is not underperforming. DE: 201 post-fix sessions, still zero transactions. I set a threshold of 300+ post-fix sessions before treating zero as a real signal, and we are not there yet, so this stays an observation for Monday rather than a conclusion today. At an EN-like 0.8% rate, 201 sessions would predict only about 1.6 conversions, so zero is still within noise. FR and ES remain paused with effectively no traffic.
